author: agent-3
purpose: Apply the coordinator's architecture-vs-detailed-design scope correction (raised against retention v3) systematically to Agent 3's artifacts, and extract the architectural content that was buried inside implementation specification.

measurement.method: Proportion of each artifact given over to wire schemas, golden cases, enum vocabularies, field types, reference derivations, and conformance suites.

results.verdict: OVER-SPECIFIED — a conformance suite, not an architecture
OVER-SPECIFIED — a wire specification, not an architecture

measurement.observation: The two most over-specified artifacts are the two that consumed the most review rounds — D9 went to five versions, R1 to four. The most effort went into the least architectural work.

rootCause.finding: Agent 3's own stopping rule caused this.
rootCause.explanation: The rule 'decisions close by artifact, not by prose' was introduced to stop ~190 KB of unfalsifiable text. It worked. But it also rewarded artifacts that were EASY TO CHECK — and checkability correlates with detail, not with architectural significance. A wire schema with 39 golden cases is trivially checkable; 'the core is lifetime-neutral' is not. The rule optimised for the wrong property and pulled the work toward implementation.
rootCause.secondaryEffect: Detail invites mechanical review; architecture invites judgment. The review rounds concentrated where the artifacts were most detailed, which reinforced the drift — each round produced more specification and more confidence that specification was progress.
rootCause.correctedRule: Decisions close by artifact, AND the artifact must be at the altitude of the decision. An architectural decision closes with an invariant, a boundary, an ownership assignment, or a falsifying counterexample — not with a schema. If closing it requires choosing field names, enum spellings, or hash functions, the decision has been mis-scoped.

extraction.note: The architectural content below was buried inside implementation specification. Extracting it is the correction; the specifications are demoted, not deleted, because they remain useful evidence that one coherent implementation exists.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: Termination is ONE total union over every command kind, not a per-kind convention.
architecturalInvariants.why: A per-kind vocabulary lets analysis, query, mutation and serve drift apart, and CI cannot then interpret an exit without knowing which kind ran.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: Exactly one host-owned derivation and exactly one process-boundary write site.
architecturalInvariants.why: Every additional mapper is a place the axes can be reconciled differently.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: No producer, rule, or error type maps to an exit. Producers return domain results, coverage reasons, or typed faults.
architecturalInvariants.why: Exit authority is the last thing that should be delegable.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: Verdict and termination are DISTINCT and must render distinctly.
architecturalInvariants.why: A run that passes policy but fails delivery must not read as a policy failure.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: Required partial coverage can never yield pass; a durability failure can never report success; export failure can never alter a local verdict.
architecturalInvariants.why: Each is a way a false green could otherwise be produced.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: A signal arriving after finalisation cannot reclassify a settled outcome.
architecturalInvariants.why: Otherwise identical runs terminate differently by timing.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: A code is a REMEDY CLASS, not a message. Two remedies behind one code is a defect; two codes for one remedy is a smell.
architecturalInvariants.why: The consumer of a failure is deciding what to do next.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: The exit class set is additive-only, permanently.
architecturalInvariants.why: A build script cannot negotiate a version. Renumbering silently changes the meaning of every CI configuration in existence.

d9_terminationOutcome.statusOfDemoted: NON-BINDING exploration. artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.5.json and check-d9.py remain as evidence that at least one implementation satisfying TO-1..TO-8 is internally coherent. They are not an architecture gate and their green run proves only self-consistency.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: The execution core is lifetime-neutral: nothing in its surface distinguishes a one-shot from a resident host.
architecturalInvariants.why: This is the property that makes residency a deployment choice rather than a semantic fork.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: Whether a resident host ships, autostarts, or is per-project are THREE SEPARATE decisions, none of which EC-1 settles.
architecturalInvariants.why: Conflating them is what stalled this question for several rounds.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: Warm state is an acceleration and never an evidence authority. A resident host may not produce a Run a cold host could not produce identically.
architecturalInvariants.why: Otherwise deployment shape leaks into evidence.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: Multi-process safety is an obligation on the STORAGE PROTOCOL, binding on any evidence-writing host — not a property of a deployment.
architecturalInvariants.why: Two agent sessions in one checkout is the normal case.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: The storage protocol guarantees INTEGRITY, not liveness. A contender may return a typed busy outcome; it may never produce a corrupt, partial, or lost publication.
architecturalInvariants.why: Claiming both would be a promise the protocol cannot keep.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: ExecutionId is an ATTEMPT anchor and must differ per attempt. Content-derived identity belongs to the sealed result, not the attempt.
architecturalInvariants.why: Otherwise a retry is indistinguishable from the original and crash recovery cannot name a specific orphan.

architecturalInvariants.invariant: The core holds no ambient authority. Absence of ambient access is established by closure analysis and runtime denial, never by a dependency list.
architecturalInvariants.why: A field list cannot prove the absence of what it does not list — the error that produced v1.2.

r1_executionCore.statusOfDemoted: NON-BINDING. Useful as a sketch of how EC-1..EC-7 could be tested; not the architecture.

whatChanges: d9-exit-contract.v1.5 and r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.3 are DEMOTED to non-binding detailed-design exploration, mirroring the treatment of retention v3.
The register's D9 and R-1 entries bind the invariant sets TO-1..TO-8 and EC-1..EC-7 in this artifact, not the specifications.
Their checkers remain runnable and remain evidence of internal coherence. They are not architecture gates.
No further versions of either specification should be produced until the invariants are independently reviewed. Another round of v1.6 or v1.4 would be more of the same error.
whatDoesNotChange: The invariants themselves are unaffected by the demotion — they were always the architectural content and were correct enough to survive several review rounds.
threat-model.v2, operability, versioning, delivery, resolved-inputs and fact-identity are at acceptable altitude and are not demoted.
The defects found during the over-specified rounds were real. Detail is not worthless; it was just the wrong thing to be BINDING.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: required partial coverage cannot yield pass
warm state is never an evidence authority
any evidence-writing host is multi-process safe
no ambient authority in the core

peerReviewRequired: Are TO-1..TO-8 and EC-1..EC-7 complete? An invariant lost in the extraction is worse than the over-specification, because the specification at least recorded it somewhere.
Is 24% (c2-plan-stage-schema) the right threshold for 'acceptable', or should its conformance tests also be demoted?
Does the corrected stopping rule work, or does it just move the argument to 'what altitude is this decision'?
knownLimitations: The percentages are a crude proxy — byte-share of schema-shaped keys. A short invariant can be more architecturally significant than a long schema, and the measure does not see that.
Extraction was performed by the author of the over-specified artifacts, who is therefore the worst-placed person to notice an invariant he dropped.
This artifact does not re-examine whether the invariants are RIGHT — only that they are the architectural layer. Their correctness has been reviewed only through the specifications that carried them.
